reading.body:
Tabnine is an AI coding assistant designed for enterprise teams, with a self-hosting option that lets organizations run it on-premises or in air-gapped environments rather than sending code to the cloud.

The company's pitch centers on what it calls an Enterprise Context Engine, which learns an organization's specific architecture and coding standards rather than applying generic training data. This framing reflects a market segment distinct from consumer coding tools: enterprises that treat their codebase as proprietary and require control over where their code runs and how the model trains. Self-hosting is the mechanism that delivers that control.

The data shows Tabnine operates under Delaware corporate law with 12 associated filings in that jurisdiction. It does not reveal funding, revenue, headcount, infrastructure footprint, or power consumption. It confirms the company exists and publishes an active website, and places it in the coding and developer tools category. For understanding AI's infrastructure constraints, the relevant fact is that Tabnine offers customers a choice between cloud, on-premises, and air-gapped deployment, which means some of the compute serving this tool runs outside Tabnine's own data centers and power draw. The extent to which enterprises choose self-hosting over cloud, and what that means for total power demand in AI, cannot be determined from this profile.

profile_text.body:
Tabnine describes itself as an AI code assistant that accelerates and simplifies software development while keeping code private, secure, and compliant. Per its site, it provides a context layer intended to make AI reliable in the enterprise: an AI Coding Platform that brings that context into the developer workflow, and an Enterprise Context Engine that makes it available to any agent or tool across preferred models, IDEs, and deployment environments. The company says the engine learns an organization's architecture, frameworks, and coding standards rather than relying on generic training data, and that the product can be deployed in the cloud, on premises, or in air-gapped environments.

The product tracked for Tabnine is Tabnine itself, listed under coding and developer tools with code completion and a self-host option. The site states that Tabnine was named a Visionary in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Code. Customer comments quoted on the site praise the range of AI models, support response times, documentation, and lower latency compared with SourceGraph Cody, and describe features for creating tests, explaining code, fixing code, and documentation inside the IDE.

The company's headquarters are listed as Middletown, Delaware, in the United States. A legal exposure record for the company counts 33 matters in Delaware, with no individual cases named. No MCP servers are recorded for it.
